profile.profile_long: the sources do not describe a dance tradition named hinde. Rather, they document the 1979 studio album Dancing Up a Storm by the husband-and-wife duo The Raes. Released on A&M Records in March 1979, the album featured hit singles including 'A Little Lovin' (Keeps the Doctor Away)' and 'I Only Wanna Get Up and Dance'. The project peaked at number 161 on Billboard magazine's Top 200 chart. Production for the album was handled by Harry Hinde, with arrangements by David Van De Pitte. Recording took place at Manta Sound in Toronto, Canada, while mixing occurred at Mom & Pop's Company Store in Studio City, California, and Sigma Sound Studios in New York City. Personnel credits include bass by Bob Babbitt, drums by Charles Collins, guitars by Bruce Nazarian and Paul Sabu, keyboards by Carlton Kent, and percussion by Jim Maelen and Paulinho da Costa. Wikidata classifies the release as an album within the disco genre. No historical, technical, or cultural details regarding a dance tradition are available in the source material.
